question: p-solar
unit: sum (whole 30 kWp array, ~60 panels, ~120 m2 panel area, Auckland site, GST exclusive)

band.unit: sum (whole 30 kWp array, ~60 panels, ~120 m2 panel area, Auckland site, GST exclusive)
band.basis: Auckland, NZD, GST exclusive. Built by adding non-overlapping components: mounting system $7,155-$16,235 (rails, brackets, clamps and fasteners from NZ supplier pages, plus QV roofer labour), strengthening $1,884-$3,330 (QV proprietary purlins DHS 150/15 to 250/15 for 40-50 m, plus an allowance for bolts, cleats and fixings the QV purlin rate excludes), design and PS1 $1,500-$2,800 (published per-building structural assessment schedule). No QV solar-mounting row exists, so the largest component rests on fetched supplier prices, not a QV rate or a project quote; install hours and purlin quantity are my estimates. Confidence LOW, and the band is deliberately wide: the low end is itemised trade-rate hardware, the high end is branded retail kit pricing (a 4-panel GridFree kit is $700, i.e. $175/panel, or $10,500 for 60 panels). Excludes GST, preliminaries, margin, all electrical work, roof sheet replacement/recoating, scaffolding/edge protection/roof access and consent fees, per the fixed scope.

band.unit: sum (whole 30 kWp array: 60 panels, ~120 m2, mounting + one-third purlin strengthening + design/PS1)
band.basis: GST-exclusive lump sum built from cited QV CostBuilder rows (proprietary purlins and bolts, steel erector labour rate) plus fetched NZ vendor prices for proprietary racking components and a fetched NZ structural consultancy fee schedule for the design/PS1. Three rejectable parts: MOUNTING SYSTEM low $5,516 / high $9,114; STRENGTHENING (purlins + bolts) low $1,685 / high $3,138; DESIGN (PS1 + wind calculation) low $2,340 / high $4,180. Excludes GST, preliminaries, margin, PV modules, inverters, cabling and electrical work, roof sheet works, scaffolding/edge protection and consent fees, per scope. Cross-check: a racking vendor benchmark of '$0.08-$0.15 per watt' (novamounting.com/blog/solar-racking-system-cost-2026, source-8) implies $2,400-$4,500 for 30 kWp of racking supply, below my NZ retail-based build-up; that vendor page also notes wind region and uplift requirements push racking cost up, which is the case here.

Lump sum for the exact scope, Auckland, GST exclusive. Mounting system $6,497-$14,555 + supplementary purlins and bolts $1,448-$2,629 + design and PS1 $2,500-$4,000. Sydney: no - Auckland. Mounting hardware is priced from NZ published vendor prices (Fazcorp $84.95/4.75 m rail, $4.95 brackets, $4.95 clamps; GridFree/KSENG $85/2.4 m rail, $19 L-feet, $17 clamps) at quantities from GridFree's published 4-panel kit BOM (2.4 m rail, 2 L-feet, 3 clamps per panel), with installation labour at the QV Auckland roofer rate; strengthening from QV proprietary purlin and bolt rows; design fee from an Auckland engineering firm's published schedule. The band is wide (about 2x) for one reason: NZ published hardware prices are retail/DIY level, while the only commercial-scale benchmark found is below them - Nova Mounting states 'In 2026 Australia, solar racking typically adds around $0.08-$0.15 per watt' and shows $0.10 to $0.20/W supplied for 30-100 kW arrays (~$3,000-$6,000 for 30 kWp) (source-7). A contractor quote for 60 panels should therefore sit in the lower half of this band; the top end is what the scope costs if every item is bought at retail singles. Allowances are under 5% of the total, so the band is rate-driven. Excludes GST, preliminaries, margin, modules/inverters/cabling, roof sheet work, scaffolding/edge protection and consent fees, as instructed.
